channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Saints GM Mickey Loomis said Chris Olave (clot) has no restrictions and is now “full go.”
9NEWS’ Mike Klis reports Ben Powers took a “significant” pay cut to stay with the Broncos.
item.description: Powers played through a “previously undisclosed” Lisfranc injury over the final five games of the season, and Klis notes that “Powers refused to have an MRI exam on his foot until the season ended, telling the Broncos’ training staff he could play through it and they could examine it later.” Football players: They aren’t like us. Powers will reportedly have a training camp battle with Alex Palczewski to start at left guard. It was reported earlier this offseason that Powers wasn’t taking a pay cut by Klis, but the Broncos apparently changed their mind.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Steelers GM Omar Khan said Broderick Jones (neck) is medically cleared to practice.
item.description: He did say they’d be “smart” about him and where he is strength and conditioning wise, so Jones may wind up taking a longer build up. But overall, this is a fairly positive update about a player who we weren’t completely sure would play in 2026 as recently as a few months ago.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports Zach Charbonnet (knee) is a “potential close call” to be ready for Week 1.
item.description: Breer continues that the Seahawks are “going to be smart with him.” We’d be floored by a Week 1 return given Charbonnet suffered a torn ACL just last January, but the Seahawks haven’t really put out a real timetable on his status. Seahawks coach Mike McDaniel said in June that “everything’s possible” when asked about Charbonnet playing in Week 1, but didn’t elaborate much on the odds. It does sound like even if Charbonnet is placed on the reserve/PUP list at the end of camp, he’d have a real shot to play in October.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Will Levis and Mitch Trubisky will have a competition to be Cam Ward’s backup.
item.description: Levis, who has been in trade rumors at times this year, would appear to be the favorite to be released or traded from where we sit this offseason. We doubt that Brian Daboll brought in his old charge Trubisky this offseason just to instantly release him, but the fact that they’re positioning it as a real battle at least opens the possibility. Expect to see plenty of Levis in the preseason this year.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Colts GM Chris Ballard said he’d “love to have” Jonathan Taylor and Quenton Nelson “long-term,” then added “we’ll see.”
item.description: Indianapolis Star’s Joel A. Erickson puts it this way: “the Colts also find themselves at a crossroads. Ballard is headed into the final year of his contract; if Indianapolis does not win, the Colts could be headed for organizational change. A superstar running back might not fit in a rebuild.” It will be very interesting to see if Taylor holds in without a new contract. Ballard spent a lot of his press conference saying his own contract status — he’s a lame duck GM — won’t affect his ability to make long-term decisions. In his own words: We’ll see.-Rivers McCown

item.title: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes “it’s fair to be optimistic” that Malik Nabers (knee) will play in Week 1.
item.description: Nabers will “have a reduced workload early in camp” and avoiding the PUP list was “a promising first step, but it’s not the final checkpoint” per Duggan. That’s the bad news, but the overall trend is going enough in the right direction that Duggan believes Nabers could play right away. These things can shift fast — one rough practice could change a whole tone — but guarded optimism is probably the right way to characterize this update.-Rivers McCown

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports Steston Bennett is getting the “first crack” with the ones when Matthew Stafford rests.
item.description: Atkins doesn’t seem impressed with Bennett (who has “fallen victim to a couple of greedy mistakes”) or Ty Simpson (“isn’t going downfield much”) early in camp and suggests that the unsigned Jimmy Garoppolo could just be a phone call away if Simpson isn’t able to win the QB2 job. We’ll see what happens, but Garoppolo lingering as a free agent could keep some upside injury runouts off the table for Simpson this year.-Rivers McCown

item.title: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell reports the Chiefs are “eager” to test Patrick Mahomes’ (knee) limits at the start of training camp.
item.description: Mahomes is wearing a brace — he doesn’t seem particularly comfortable with it yet, per Newell — and he’s also still favoring the leg a bit. Neither of those are very surprising observations, but it says a lot that the Chiefs are trying to get a good gauge on where Mahomes is right away. Per Newell, Mahomes took a lot more under-center reps as well, which could signal an offensive shift for the unit towards something that’s better for Kenneth Walker.-Rivers McCown

item.title: Steelers placed CB Joey Porter (undisclosed) on the active/PUP list.
item.description: It’s unknown what the injury is here, as Porter was not mentioned in an injury rundown by GM Omar Khan earlier this morning. More information to come when it is available. Porter was a potential hold-in (as he was at OTAs) as he tries to work on a contract extension with the team.-Rivers McCown
